alignments.note: Waw of the consecutive form takes And; the verb takes the verb (rule 14).
כֹּל as all.
Construct noun men; no article morpheme stands in the chain, so the supplied the belongs to the nominal expression it determines (rules 15, 29).
Nomen rectum takes the of-expression (rule 19).
Verb answered; its unit stands apart from its waw because English puts the subject first (rule 25).
The ASV renders the object bare, answered the men of Israel, so this עַל keeps nothing (rule 40).
Construct noun men with its supplied the (rules 15, 29).
Nomen rectum takes the of-expression (rule 19).
Causal כִּי as Because.
Article takes the written the (rule 15).
Noun king, the clause's explicit subject, taking only its own English (rule 20).

Predicate adjective of a verbless clause: the construction-supplied copula joins the predicate (rule 20), and the ASV renders קָרוֹב by the phrase near of kin, whose lexeme is carried by near (rule 31).
Preposition to (rule 11).
Suffix as object pronoun; the ASV writes us where the suffix is singular, and rule 18 aligns the pronoun that is written.
לָמָּה rendered by the one English word wherefore: rule 30 fusion, headed on the interrogative. Recorded noncompositional, with the chapter's five other לָמָה units.

Waw rendered by the connective then, written after the interrogative; distance is not evidence against it (rules 14, 51). The competing reading gives then to the emphatic זֶּה and marks the waw unrepresented; I take the waw because rule 14 reads the ASV's connective off a waw that is present, and then is such a connective.
The deictic זֶּה of לָמָּה זֶּה has no English word of its own here; then was placed on the waw above (rule 22).
The impersonal חָרָה לְ is recast as a personal are ye angry: the verb keeps the copular auxiliary and the lexical predicate, discontinuous around the subject pronoun (rules 17, 25), headed on angry.
Under the personal recasting the suffix takes the English subject pronoun (rule 40).
The recasting leaves this לְ no English word (rule 40).
Preposition rendered for (rule 11).
The demonstrative pronoun is what the ASV's this realizes; rule 41 gives a determiner to the article only where no other morpheme licenses it, and here זֶּה does.
Noun matter.
The ASV writes no the for the phrase, only the demonstrative, which the present זֶּה takes (rules 29, 41).
The agreement article on the demonstrative likewise has no English (rules 29, 47).
The fronted question auxiliary have belongs to the interrogative particle (rule 17).
Cognate infinitive absolute rendered by the distinct intensifier at all, a single two-word intensifying rendering, headed on the word carrying it (rule 56).
Finite cognate verb keeps its subject pronoun and lexical verb (rules 56, 17); its auxiliary went to the interrogative particle.
מִן rendered by at in the ASV's recasting at the king's cost (rule 11).
Article takes the written the (rule 15).
Noun king, rendered as an English possessive by the recasting.

No morpheme licenses cost: the Hebrew reads only from the king, and this noun is the ASV's supplied complement of its recasting (rule 30). Folding it into the king's unit would put a word inside a rendering no source morpheme licenses.

The אִם of the second disjunctive question takes the or the ASV writes for it; rule 17's fronted-auxiliary reading does not apply because a connective is written here and the auxiliary hath belongs to the verb.

Cognate infinitive absolute takes the distinct intensifier any, the interrogative counterpart of the at all written for the parallel אָכוֹל אָכַלְנוּ (rule 56). The competing reading marks this morpheme unrepresented and any added; I take the intensifier because the ASV writes it in the slot the first question's intensifier occupies.
The Niphal is recast as an active with a supplied subject pronoun and auxiliary, all belonging to the verb (rule 17), headed on the lexical verb.
Dative לְ rendered as a bare English indirect object, given us, leaving the preposition nothing (rule 40).
Suffix as object pronoun (rules 18, 40).

No morpheme licenses gift: the clause has only the verb, its preposition and suffix, and the infinitive absolute, each with its own rendering. The supplied object stands beside those renderings rather than inside one of them (rules 30, 42).

review_notes: Only the status of the לָמָּה unit changed; its edges and heads are as the verse pass returned them, and no other unit was touched.
Every source and target ID is partitioned exactly once; six unrepresented units and two added units (cost, gift), both supplied nouns of the ASV's recasting of the two rhetorical questions.
The two interrogative clauses are read differently on purpose: הֶ takes the fronted have under rule 17, while אִם takes the or the ASV actually writes, leaving hath with its verb.
this is placed on the demonstrative זֶּה rather than on either article, since rule 41 gives a determiner to the article only where no other morpheme licenses it.
